text:
Ravi Quillfeather (People Operations Lead): Thanks for the revised proposal. I went through it with Mirela line by line, and I'll give you the numbers so there's no ambiguity.
Rep: Please.
Ravi Quillfeather (People Operations Lead): Your quote for 176 employees comes to roughly thirty-eight dollars per employee per month. That's about eighty thousand a year once you add the implementation fee. We have a ceiling of sixty thousand for this whole category. That was set in the budget cycle in August.
Mirela Santangelo (Finance Director): And I can't move that number. I looked. If I take it from the facilities line, I'm answering to the CEO in January.
Rep: Did you get a comparison from someone else?
Ravi Quillfeather (People Operations Lead): Yes. I'm not going to name them, but a smaller vendor came in at twenty-seven per head per month. So, call it fifty-seven thousand a year, all in. It's thinner. Fewer reports, no dedicated rep. But it's inside the number.
Mirela Santangelo (Finance Director): Twenty-three thousand a year is twenty-three thousand a year. Over three years that's nearly seventy.
Rep: What if we phased the modules?
Ravi Quillfeather (People Operations Lead): I did ask myself that. But phasing just moves the cost. Payroll by itself would still be around thirty a head, so we'd save, what, maybe eight dollars? Still above.
Mirela Santangelo (Finance Director): We liked the product. It's the annual cost.
Ravi Quillfeather (People Operations Lead): Right. If your pricing moves next year, call me.

Emeka Ibarra (VP of People): Hey, yeah, thanks for calling back. I, uh, I should've called you first, honestly.
Rep: No problem. What's the update?
Emeka Ibarra (VP of People): So, okay, we started with Tallyhold. Last week. Signed the pilot, they've got a kickoff scheduled.
Rep: Can I ask what happened?
Emeka Ibarra (VP of People): It's the wait, mostly. You and I talked, what, the second of the month? And then the demo was eight days later. Eight days! And in that time Dariusz was on me every day, saying are we doing this or not, and Tallyhold's rep just showed up with a calendar open. So by the time you did the demo, which was good, I'm not saying it wasn't, we were already, kind of, halfway in the door over there.
Dariusz Valdivia (VP Finance): I had a budget meeting coming. I wanted a vendor lined up.
Emeka Ibarra (VP of People): Right. So. It's just timing. I feel bad.
Rep: I understand. Thanks for telling me.
Emeka Ibarra (VP of People): If it doesn't work out, I'll call.

Subject: Update on our decision

Hi, Emeka from Redfern Freight. Wanted to follow up in writing. We've gone ahead with another provider. The eight days between our first call and the demo meant we'd already started elsewhere by the time we saw yours. Thanks for your time and for the thoughtful walkthrough.

Best,
Emeka

Tobias Quillfeather (Head of HR): You said you wanted the update. We went with Corvane.
Rep: Thank you for telling me. What happened?
Tobias Quillfeather (Head of HR): Twelve days. First call to demo, twelve days. By then Kwame had already sat through Corvane's demo. Twice. We'd pretty much moved on.
Kwame Santangelo (Compliance Lead): They called me back the same day. Every time.
Tobias Quillfeather (Head of HR): The calendar slipped. I get it, you're busy. But I'm busy too. When I'm ready to buy, I buy.
Rep: Was the demo itself what you expected?
Tobias Quillfeather (Head of HR): It was fine. Good, even. It was just late. I'd already told our partners we were switching.
Kwame Santangelo (Compliance Lead): Price was a bit better over there too. Not by a lot.
Tobias Quillfeather (Head of HR): Small thing. The wait was the thing.
Rep: I understand.
Tobias Quillfeather (Head of HR): Okay. Good luck.

Ingrid Oyelaran (HR Generalist): I'll give you the decision first. We're not buying.
Rep: Okay. Can I ask why?
Ingrid Oyelaran (HR Generalist): Reporting. Specifically what our board wants.
Yuki Zeller (General Manager): I'll take that. I'm the one who sits in the board meeting.
Rep: Please.
Yuki Zeller (General Manager): Every quarter our investors want a labor cost view. Cost per hire by department. Against plan. Plus the mix of contractors versus employees. And it's never the same ask twice. Last quarter it was overtime as a share of payroll, by team lead. The quarter before, it was raises by tenure.
Ingrid Oyelaran (HR Generalist): I build those by hand today. Exports into spreadsheets. It takes me two days.
Rep: And what did you see in the demo?
Yuki Zeller (General Manager): A report library. Good one. Maybe thirty reports. Fixed. You can filter, you can export. You can't build your own view.
Ingrid Oyelaran (HR Generalist): I asked three times. Can I add a field. Can I group by something else. Can I save it. The answer was no, no, not yet.
Yuki Zeller (General Manager): That's the whole point of this project. If I'm still exporting to a spreadsheet, nothing has changed.
Rep: Anything else?
Ingrid Oyelaran (HR Generalist): No. Payroll was clean. Taxes were fine. Price was fine. I want that on the record.
Yuki Zeller (General Manager): Reporting. That's the one.
Rep: Understood. Thanks for being clear.
Yuki Zeller (General Manager): If you build it, tell me. I'll look again.

Priya Okonkwo (HR Director): Hi there, sorry, I'm in the car, the Bluetooth is awful, can you hear me okay? Greta's on the other line.
Rep: Loud and clear.
Priya Okonkwo (HR Director): Great. So I wanted to circle back on our question list, the one from last week. I've been thinking about it all weekend, which is sad.
Rep: Let's go through it.
Priya Okonkwo (HR Director): Okay, so, we've got people in four states now, and one of the things that keeps me up is, I've got a technician who lives in Kentucky and works in our Ohio office. Does your system figure out that reciprocity thing, so she isn't getting Kentucky and Ohio both taken out? Because last time she had both and she was, rightly, furious.
Rep: In that case, I'd want to confirm with our tax team how the reciprocity certificate gets recorded.
Priya Okonkwo (HR Director): That's what you said last time. We'd have to check.
Greta Brannigan (Compliance Lead): And the other one. When somebody moves mid-year, say Indiana to Illinois in August, how does the withholding split? Who files the changes with the state? Are we on the hook?
Rep: Honestly, I don't have a clean answer there. We'd have to check with the compliance group.
Priya Okonkwo (HR Director): And I know it's silly, but those are the two things. If the tax part isn't airtight we can't, you know. Price, yes, I noticed it's a little higher than we figured, but that's not it. We'd pay it.
Greta Brannigan (Compliance Lead): We can't guess on this.
Priya Okonkwo (HR Director): So we're going with Corvane. They walked us through both examples on the call. I'll send you a note.

Subject: Our decision

Hi,

Thank you again for all the time you and your team gave us. We've decided to go with Corvane. The deciding piece for Greta and me was how payroll taxes get handled across our four states, particularly the Kentucky and Ohio reciprocity situation and mid-year moves. We needed firm answers and, on those two, we didn't get them. The rest of what we saw was good, and the price was reasonable. We'd happily look again if that area develops.

Best,
Priya

Odalys Dunmore (HR Director): Let's get to it. I have a hard stop at three.
Rep: Sure. Where did the team land?
Odalys Dunmore (HR Director): We're passing. Hollis, you want to say it?
Hollis Zeller (Controller): Payroll tax. We have people in seven states. Two weeks ago I asked about Pennsylvania. We have two employees there, in different townships, and the local earned income tax goes to different collectors depending on where they live. How does your system pick the collector, and who files?
Rep: I believe we handle the filing at the state level. For the local collector, I'd have to check.
Hollis Zeller (Controller): That's what I heard. Second one. We're hiring our first person in Tennessee next month. Who registers us with the state for unemployment, and how fast?
Rep: We'd have to check on the timeline.
Odalys Dunmore (HR Director): Look, we don't need perfect. We need confident. If I can't tell my CEO who files what in a new state, I can't put payroll on this.
Hollis Zeller (Controller): Price is a little above where I thought. Whatever. I'd pay it.
Odalys Dunmore (HR Director): So that's it. Tax handling.
Rep: Understood. Thanks for being direct.
Odalys Dunmore (HR Director): Appreciate the time.

Marisol Cadogan (COO): Good afternoon. Thank you both for joining. I will be candid, as I think you deserve that.
Rep: I'd appreciate it.
Marisol Cadogan (COO): We have not chosen Lanternmere HR. We operate in eight states, and the payroll tax question has not been resolved to our satisfaction. Wren, would you summarise?
Wren Zeller (Payroll Manager): Certainly. Two specific scenarios. First, we have a clinician working remotely from Oregon, and Oregon has the statewide transit tax in addition to the usual withholding. I asked whether your system calculates and remits that. The answer I received was that you would need to confirm.
Rep: Yes, I recall.
Wren Zeller (Payroll Manager): Second, Colorado. The family leave insurance premiums are split between employer and employee, and the rate changes. I asked who updates the rate and who files the quarterly report. Again, the response was that you would have to check.
Marisol Cadogan (COO): I do not want to be unfair. The people we met were knowledgeable in other areas. The product demonstration was good. Pricing, if I may, is somewhat higher than we expected, but it is not what this is about. We would have paid it.
Rep: Is there anything that would change the outcome?
Marisol Cadogan (COO): A written description of how each of those is handled, state by state, would have changed it. We could not get to that point. And, in fairness, the project was already slowing down internally. Our finance director asked to delay anything non-essential until the new year. So the timing was not ideal either.
Wren Zeller (Payroll Manager): But the tax handling, mainly.
Marisol Cadogan (COO): Yes. That is the main matter.
Rep: Thank you. I'll pass that to our product team.
Marisol Cadogan (COO): Please do. We wish you well.

Subject: Following our call

Marisol, thank you for the candid feedback. I've shared the Oregon transit tax and Colorado premium questions with our payroll tax team, and I'll send written answers when they're ready, in case it's useful later. Wishing you and Wren the best.

Nadia Thorsen (VP of People): Hi! Oh, it's so good to see your face again. Did you get any of that rain? We got, I think, three solid days of it, and my dog has opinions.
Rep: A bit of it. Hope the dog's coping.
Nadia Thorsen (VP of People): He's fine. He's dramatic. Priya, say hi.
Priya Quillfeather (Payroll Manager): Hi! Hello. Nice to see you.
Rep: Great to see you both. I wanted to hear where things stand.
Nadia Thorsen (VP of People): Right, right, so I wanted to be the one to tell you. We've decided we're going a different direction. And I just want to say, it's been such a pleasure working with you.
Rep: Thank you, Nadia. I appreciate you telling me directly. Is there anything you'd be willing to share about the decision?
Nadia Thorsen (VP of People): Oh, you know, it's just, we're making a change. That's really where we landed. It was a team conversation and everybody was, you know, thoughtful about it.
Priya Quillfeather (Payroll Manager): Everybody on your side was lovely. Honestly. I told my husband, they were the nicest people.
Nadia Thorsen (VP of People): They really were. Genuinely. I don't want you to take this as anything. It's a change we're making, and that's all.
Rep: I understand. If you ever want to revisit, our door is open.
Nadia Thorsen (VP of People): That's so kind of you. I'll keep your card. I mean it. Oh, and you should come out to see our place sometime, we have this little patio now, we got string lights and everything.
Rep: I'd love that.
Priya Quillfeather (Payroll Manager): Bring a sweater. It gets chilly.
Nadia Thorsen (VP of People): It does. Well, I'll let you go. Take care of yourself, okay?
Rep: You too, both of you.

Bastian Delacroix (VP of People): Sorry I'm late. Back to back since seven. I'll tell you the truth, I'm running on coffee and spite today.
Rep: No worries. Thanks for taking the call.
Bastian Delacroix (VP of People): So. Where are we. We're not moving on this. Not now. And I want to tell you it's not about you, because that sounds like a line, but I really mean it.
Rep: What changed?
Bastian Delacroix (VP of People): Two weeks ago the board told us we might be acquired. Might. They won't say by who. So Nadia pulled every discretionary project, and this is one of them. Payroll and HR systems get swapped out by the buyer anyway, or that's the assumption.
Nadia Zeller (CFO): Or they leave us alone and we've lost a quarter. I don't know. I can't justify a three-year commitment when I can't tell you what the company looks like in March.
Bastian Delacroix (VP of People): Yeah. And, I mean, I put in a lot of work on this. Those thirteen days before the demo, I spent half of that chasing people internally. I got the sponsor, got the budget slotted. It was all there. I loved the demo. Honestly, I wanted it.
Rep: And no other vendor in the picture?
Bastian Delacroix (VP of People): No. We're staying on what we have. It's clunky. Our payroll person does a lot of manual corrections. But it's what we have. Nobody's even looking at alternatives. Everything is on hold.
Nadia Zeller (CFO): I'd say price was reasonable. I told Bastian that. Your product is fine. It's the situation.
Bastian Delacroix (VP of People): If the deal falls apart, or if it happens and they say keep your systems, I'll call you the next day.
Rep: I'd welcome that.
Bastian Delacroix (VP of People): I'm really tired of living in limbo. Anyway. That's where we are.

Signe Hollander (People Operations Lead): Let me give you the status with some numbers, because I know you'll be asked.
Rep: Please.
Signe Hollander (People Operations Lead): Third quarter patient volume came in eleven percent under plan. On the sixth, our CFO froze all new vendor commitments over twenty-five thousand dollars through the end of the fiscal year. Our project would have been about ninety-one thousand over three years, so it falls inside the freeze.
Ravi Yarrow (Benefits Manager): And for context, the original approval had a sponsor, our former COO, who left in October. Nobody has picked up the project. I've asked twice.
Rep: So no one else is evaluating?
Signe Hollander (People Operations Lead): Correct. No other vendor. We reviewed two options, and then we stopped reviewing. Everything is paused at this stage.
Rep: Anything about our proposal that gave you concern?
Signe Hollander (People Operations Lead): No. The demo scored well on our internal rubric, I think we gave it a thirty-four out of forty. Pricing was in range. The eleven states, that's a complication for any vendor, we knew that going in, but it didn't stop us.
Ravi Yarrow (Benefits Manager): The freeze was the issue. It's a calendar problem and a funding problem.
Signe Hollander (People Operations Lead): My guess is that we revisit in the second quarter at the earliest.
Rep: I'll check in then.
Signe Hollander (People Operations Lead): That works.

Subject: Pausing our evaluation

Hello,

A short note to confirm what we discussed. Our evaluation of payroll and HR platforms is paused indefinitely following the vendor spending freeze. We haven't selected anyone. Please keep our materials on file, and I'll contact you when we reopen the project, likely in the second quarter.

Regards,
Signe Hollander

Sunniva Galbraith (HR Director): I'm going to be honest with you, I haven't slept well since the demo. Not because of you. Because of what I couldn't answer for my own people.
Rep: Tell me.
Sunniva Galbraith (HR Director): Twelve states. That's our reality, because we've got remote staff scattered everywhere. And I asked you how it works when someone lives in Maryland and works out of our D.C. office. Who gets the withholding? You said you'd get back to me. It's been, what, three weeks.
Rep: I remember, and I'm sorry we haven't closed it out.
Sunniva Galbraith (HR Director): And the second one. A teacher moves from New York to Florida in the middle of the year, mid-semester, and we've got to stop one state's tax and start the other, and I need to know the system does it right. Not that it might. That it does. Your answer was, we'd have to check with the tax folks.
Ravi Jessamy (General Manager): And we're a school network. Auditors come in. If we get a state notice, I'm the one calling them.
Sunniva Galbraith (HR Director): The price, fine. It's a little high. I said that once. But I'd pay it if I trusted the tax side. I don't, yet. So I'm not going to sign something I can't defend.
Rep: Understood.
Ravi Jessamy (General Manager): I don't want to put it on you personally. You were straight with us.
Sunniva Galbraith (HR Director): Anyway. We'll look elsewhere. I'm just tired, to be honest.

Wren Brannigan (HR Generalist): Hi, so, I was going to send an email, but then I thought, no, call, that's more polite, and then I thought, what if she's busy, but here we are.
Rep: Glad you called.
Wren Brannigan (HR Generalist): So, um, it's a pause from us. Mostly. We've got staff in five states and the tax questions, they're the thing I couldn't get past. Like, in Indiana the county tax depends on where you lived on January first, right? And we have a bus driver who moved over to Illinois in June. I asked you how the system handles that, and I think the answer was, we'd have to check.
Rep: That's right, I owed you an answer.
Wren Brannigan (HR Generalist): And then reciprocity between Illinois and Wisconsin for our two teachers who commute, I asked about that too. Same thing.
Priya Ibarra (Head of Finance): And price is fine, I'll say that. It was the tax part.
Wren Brannigan (HR Generalist): Also, the superintendent kind of put a hold on new projects, with the levy vote coming. So, that too. But, you know, smaller thing. The taxes were my main worry.

Wren Eastwood (HR Director): Thanks for the time. I'll keep it organized. Three points.
Rep: Go ahead.
Wren Eastwood (HR Director): First, to review the process. We had four conversations with your team since September. Two with you, one with your implementation lead, one with security. Soren sat in on three of them.
Soren Rourke (Compliance Lead): Three of four. I missed the security one.
Wren Eastwood (HR Director): Second, I want to put on record that your team was responsive. The longest we waited for a reply to an email was, I checked, about three hours. And the security questionnaire came back complete, forty-one pages, no blanks.
Rep: Thank you, I'll pass that along.
Wren Eastwood (HR Director): Third, and this is the part I owe you. We've decided to go in a different direction. I'm not going to dress it up. It's the direction we're taking.
Rep: Understood. Is there anything you can share about how the decision was reached?
Wren Eastwood (HR Director): The team reviewed the options and made a determination. I'd rather leave it there, if you don't mind. It's not a reflection on the people you sent us.
Soren Rourke (Compliance Lead): No. Everyone was professional.
Rep: Then I won't press. Would it be all right if I checked in down the road?
Wren Eastwood (HR Director): That's fine. Though I'd say, don't plan around it.
Rep: Fair. Thank you both.
Wren Eastwood (HR Director): Thank you. You'll get a written note from me today so it's on record.

Subject: Our decision

Dear team,

Thank you for the time and care you put into our evaluation, including the thorough security documentation. After careful consideration we have decided to go in a different direction and will not be moving forward with Lanternmere HR. Please convey our thanks to everyone involved. We wish you continued success.

Sincerely,
Wren Eastwood

Jules Hollander (VP of People): Hi! Hi hi. Can you hear me? My camera's being weird. Wren, can you, no, it's fine. There we go.
Rep: There you are. How are you?
Jules Hollander (VP of People): Good, good. Busy, but the good kind. We just got a new espresso machine in the office, which honestly has been the highlight of my quarter.
Wren Santangelo (IT Manager): It's a loud machine.
Jules Hollander (VP of People): It's very loud. Anyway. So I wanted to talk to you. I thought I should do this live, not by email.
Rep: I appreciate that.
Jules Hollander (VP of People): So we're going to be making a change. We're going a different direction, is I guess how I'd put it. And I wanted to thank you, personally, for everything you did. You were great to work with.
Rep: Thank you, Jules. If you don't mind my asking, is there anything we could have done differently?
Jules Hollander (VP of People): Oh, gosh, no. No, no. It's not like that. It's just, you know, a direction thing.
Wren Santangelo (IT Manager): The setup calls were smooth, if that helps. Nothing to report on my end.
Jules Hollander (VP of People): Right, nothing to report. We just made a call, and I feel good about it. I hope that's okay.
Rep: Of course. I'm glad it was a good experience. We'll keep your info and I'll stay out of your inbox.
Jules Hollander (VP of People): Ha, no, you're fine. Honestly, send me a note if you come across a good podcast, I'm in the market.
Rep: I'll do that.
Jules Hollander (VP of People): Perfect. Okay, I should run, someone is literally waving at me through the glass.

Amara Abernethy (Director of Operations): Okay, so, I've gone back and forth on this all week, and I think I know, but let me talk it through. The other Amara's here, which makes this confusing, so I'll be Operations Amara.
Amara Delacroix (CFO): And I'm the one with the spreadsheet.
Rep: Ha, I'll try to keep you straight. Where did you land?
Amara Abernethy (Director of Operations): We're not signing. And I really wanted to. It's the yearly cost. You came in at, what was it, twenty-two a month per person?
Amara Delacroix (CFO): Twenty-two dollars per employee per month. With three hundred thirty-nine people that's about eighty-nine and a half thousand a year. I round it to ninety.
Amara Abernethy (Director of Operations): And we budgeted, I think, sixty-five.
Amara Delacroix (CFO): Sixty-five at the top. I could stretch to seventy if I stood on one foot.
Rep: And you've seen something else in the range?
Amara Delacroix (CFO): Yes. A smaller vendor, around fifteen per head. About sixty-one thousand. It doesn't do everything. But it does payroll and time off, and that's mostly what we need.
Amara Abernethy (Director of Operations): Honestly, your product's nicer. I'd say that to anyone. It's just, twenty-eight thousand a year is, that's a person.
Amara Delacroix (CFO): It's half a person, at least. And we have five states, which I know is the thing you're built for, but we've been managing so far with the spreadsheet.
Rep: Is there flexibility if we adjusted the scope?
Amara Delacroix (CFO): I looked at that. Even stripped down it's, well, not sixty-one.

Dariusz Galbraith (VP of People): So I've got news, and I'm, hm, not thrilled to deliver it. We're going with Tallyhold.
Rep: Thanks for telling me. What led there?
Dariusz Galbraith (VP of People): Our broker, mostly. I mean, she's the one who does our benefits renewal every year. Every single year. And she came to us last month with this package, payroll, benefits, time clock, everything bundled, and she said, this is what I'd do if I were you.
Tobias Parekh (COO): And we've never regretted doing what she said.
Dariusz Galbraith (VP of People): Right. I did try to say, what about the other thing we saw? But the bundle is what she put in front of us, and she'd already talked to the carriers about it. It's, I don't know, it's easier.
Rep: Did you compare the details side by side?
Dariusz Galbraith (VP of People): Kind of? Not really. I trust her. That's the honest answer.
Rep: Understood.
Tobias Parekh (COO): Your team was good. Just so you know.
Dariusz Galbraith (VP of People): Yes. Good people.

Subject: Thank you, and our decision

Hi,

I wanted to put this in writing. We're going to move ahead with Tallyhold. Our benefits broker has handled our renewals for years and recommended their bundle, and since it's the package she brought us, we're following her lead. Tobias and I both thought your team was excellent, and I appreciate how patient you were with our questions. If our situation changes at the next renewal, I'll reach out.

Best,
Dariusz

Tobias Petrakis (COO): Thanks for taking this. I'd like to go through our reasoning with specifics, because I think it helps you more than a polite no.
Rep: I'd appreciate that.
Tobias Petrakis (COO): We have 248 employees across eight states. Roughly sixty percent are field crews who move between job sites. Dariusz handles payroll, so I'll let him walk through where we got stuck.
Dariusz Ivarsson (Payroll Manager): Two scenarios, both from our actual payroll. One. A crew based in Texas gets a job in Oklahoma for nine weeks. They're on our Texas payroll, but the work is physically in Oklahoma. I need to know when we have to start withholding for Oklahoma, whether there's a threshold, and whether we need to register before the first day. I asked on our second call and on the follow-up. The answer both times was, we would have to check.
Rep: That's accurate. I'm sorry we didn't get you something firm.
Dariusz Ivarsson (Payroll Manager): Two. State unemployment rates. Each January the states send us a rate notice, eight different notices, eight different formats. I asked who loads those, whether it's us or you, and what happens if a notice is late. You told me your team handles it, but you couldn't say how, or when, or what happens if a rate is wrong and we get a bill.
Tobias Petrakis (COO): Corvane showed us the actual workflow. A screen, a person, a turnaround number. Four business days.
Dariusz Ivarsson (Payroll Manager): That was persuasive.
Tobias Petrakis (COO): Price, to be clear. Yours is about eight percent higher. We'd have absorbed it. Dariusz was the one who said, if I can't trust the tax side, it's moot.
Rep: Fair.
Tobias Petrakis (COO): You have a good product, I want to say that. When the tax handling is as clear as the rest, call us.

Wren Nakamura (VP of People): I'll be direct. We're not going with you.
Rep: Thanks for telling me. What's behind it?
Wren Nakamura (VP of People): Payroll tax. Four states. Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Delaware, Maryland. I asked a few things. First, we have a bindery lead who lives in New Jersey and works in Pennsylvania. Reciprocity. Does the system know to stop New Jersey and take Pennsylvania? Your answer was, we'd have to check.
Nadia Cadogan (Finance Director): I asked the second one. A press operator moves from Pennsylvania to Delaware in September. When does the local tax stop, and how do you report the split on the W-2?
Rep: I didn't have a firm answer.
Nadia Cadogan (Finance Director): No. And you said you'd get back to us. We got an email four days later saying the team was still looking.
Wren Nakamura (VP of People): Brasswick showed us both situations on screen. Same call.
Rep: Understood. Was anything else a factor?
Wren Nakamura (VP of People): The wait, a little. Five days between our first call and the demo. Not a big thing. We'd already started on the Brasswick call by then.
Nadia Cadogan (Finance Director): Price was fine. I'll say that. You were right in line.
Wren Nakamura (VP of People): Tax handling is the problem. That's all. If it were solid, we'd be signing.
Rep: Thank you for the honesty.
Wren Nakamura (VP of People): Of course.

Beatrix Hartigan (Operations Manager): Oh good, you're on. I was worried I had the wrong link, I've had three wrong links today. How are you?
Rep: Doing well. Thanks for making time, Beatrix.
Beatrix Hartigan (Operations Manager): So. I wanted to tell you in person. We're going with Tallyhold, and I feel awful about it, because you've been so nice, and your demo, I told Nadia, it was the cleanest one we saw.
Nadia Castellane (Controller): It was. I'll vouch.
Rep: Thank you. Would you mind sharing how you came to the decision?
Beatrix Hartigan (Operations Manager): It's our broker, really. We've used the same broker for, gosh, twelve years? He does our health plans, our dental, he does the renewals every fall, and I basically hand him the keys. And he came back and said, here's what I'd pick, here's the bundle, payroll and benefits and the time clock, one bill. And I thought, well, I'm not going to second-guess him.
Nadia Castellane (Controller): The bundle is what he put in front of us. He'd already done the legwork with the carriers.
Beatrix Hartigan (Operations Manager): And I asked, should we wait and compare, and he said, you could, but I'd just do this. And, I mean, he's right a lot.
Rep: Is there anything we could do to change that?
Beatrix Hartigan (Operations Manager): I don't think so. It's not just me. It's what he recommended.
Nadia Castellane (Controller): It's relationship stuff.
Rep: I understand.
Beatrix Hartigan (Operations Manager): I'll be thinking of you at renewal next year though!

Bram Nakamura (Operations Manager): Hey, so, do you want the long version or the short version? Because the long version has a detour.
Rep: Whichever you'd like.

Subject: Our decision

Dear colleague,

Thank you for the proposal and the time your team gave us. After careful review, we will not be proceeding. The annual cost, at roughly $750 per employee, exceeds the ceiling our leadership approved, and we have a lower-priced alternative that fits within it. This is a matter of budget alone.

We appreciated your professionalism throughout.

Sincerely,
Casper Delacroix
COO, Fernhollow Builders

Kwame Cadogan (COO): I want to be exact with you about where we landed. We are not proceeding, and the primary reason is reporting.
Rep: Okay. Tell me more.
Kwame Cadogan (COO): Our board meets quarterly. They ask for headcount by clinic, turnover by role, overtime cost as a percentage of labor, and a three-quarter trend. In the demo you showed us the standard reports. They're fine. But when I asked to build a custom view, a cross-tab of turnover by clinic by role, the answer was that we would need to export to a spreadsheet and build it ourselves.
Rep: That is how the current reporting works, yes.
Kwame Cadogan (COO): Right. And Dariusz confirmed the same when he tested it.
Dariusz Fonseca (Payroll Manager): I tried four different layouts. I could filter, but I couldn't define my own measures. For three states and seventy-six people, that is a real limit. I would be building the board packet by hand every quarter.
Kwame Cadogan (COO): Whereas the alternative lets us configure the view once and save it. That is a material difference for me.
Rep: Understood. Were there other factors?
Kwame Cadogan (COO): One, minor. Our benefits broker had already steered us toward Tallyhold, and she handles our renewals. So that pulled in the same direction. If your reporting had matched, I'd have gone to her and argued for you.
Dariusz Fonseca (Payroll Manager): The twenty-five days before the demo didn't help the mood, but that is not the issue.
Kwame Cadogan (COO): No. It's the board reporting. That's the issue.
